content:
Apple is preparing to launch its latest flagship iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. While pricing will be a clear advantage for the Pro series, there are several other areas where the iPhone 18 Pro will outshine the more expensive Ultra model.

#1: Main Camera with Variable Aperture

The iPhone 18 Pro is reportedly getting a major main camera upgrade, including the addition of a variable aperture. The iPhone Ultra, on the other hand, is not expected to feature this.

Rumors of a variable aperture have been circulating for a while, but we still don't know exactly how Apple plans to implement it. It promises to significantly improve Portrait mode performance and deliver a deeper level of depth-of-field control. Night photography could also see notable gains.

The components required for a variable aperture are expected to be larger than the current main camera. As a result, the iPhone Ultra—with its focus on an ultra-thin design—is said to miss out on this feature.

#2: Pro Max Offers Longer Battery Life

Based on leaked regulatory information, the iPhone Ultra should deliver decent battery life. But the Pro series—specifically the iPhone 18 Pro Max—will still offer the longest battery life ever seen on an iPhone.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max is reportedly getting a physical battery roughly 10% larger than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, along with efficiency improvements from the A20 Pro and C2 chips. As a result, battery life should easily set a new record for any iPhone to date.

Due to its unique foldable design, it's hard to judge the iPhone Ultra's battery life based purely on specifications. However, the ultra-thin design and smaller physical battery will almost certainly prevent it from matching the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

#3: Face ID

For the first time in years, a flagship new iPhone model will not feature Face ID. The iPhone Ultra will offer Touch ID only.

The iPhone 18 Pro, meanwhile, will continue with the Face ID system that has been in use for nearly a decade.

Apple is reportedly unable to free up enough internal space within the iPhone Ultra's slim chassis to accommodate Face ID components. Proper support would require two sets of components—one for the outer display and another for the inner display. So when it comes to authentication, the iPhone 18 Pro will have a clear advantage.

#4: Telephoto Lens

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will remain the only models to feature a telephoto lens. The iPhone Ultra will include a main camera and an ultra-wide lens, but no telephoto lens for optical zoom.

For many users who rely on telephoto capabilities, this could be a significant difference. Especially since Apple is reportedly further enhancing the telephoto lens this year with a larger aperture.

If you're looking for the best camera system, the iPhone 18 Pro will be the obvious choice.

Bonus: The Traditional iPhone Experience

This isn't strictly a feature, but it's worth mentioning. For many users, the iPhone 18 Pro offering a "traditional" iPhone experience is itself an advantage.

The iPhone Ultra will be unlike any previous model. The size and shape of the inner and outer displays may make it feel a bit unfamiliar as an iPhone. And the need to fold and unfold it rather than simply using a single display could take some getting used to.

The iPhone in its current form is a beloved product. While foldable phones definitely have their fans, I suspect that for the average consumer—those who might never read 9to5Mac—the traditional design of the iPhone 18 Pro will be a plus for many people.

Which new iPhone model are you planning to pick up this fall? Let us know in the comments.
